language_specific.verb: Perfective; contextual imperfective partner давать. Future forms дам, даст; imperative stress да́йте. Takes an accusative object and can name the recipient in the dative; here it requests the bread.
language_specific.usage: The вы-form, извините and пожалуйста make a polite request.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; contextual imperfective partner брать. Future forms возьму, возьмёт; imperative stress возьми́. Takes an accusative object; the imperative requests that the umbrella be taken.
language_specific.usage: Петя is a familiar singular addressee; the rain supplies the reason.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; contextual imperfective partner показывать. Future forms покажу, покажет; imperative stress покажи́те. The following где-clause supplies what to show; the imperative requests one act of showing.
language_specific.usage: The вы-form is a polite request to the doctor.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; contextual imperfective partner останавливать. Future forms остановлю, остановит; imperative stress останови́те. An accusative object such as машину can be omitted when understood; the request is to stop here.
language_specific.usage: Извините and пожалуйста soften a request to stop here.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; contextual imperfective partner звонить. Future forms позвоню, позвонит; imperative stress позвони́. Takes a dative person; the imperative requests a phone call.
language_specific.usage: Врачу identifies the person to call; скорее makes the request urgent.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person plural imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; contextual imperfective partner вызывать. Future forms вызову, вызовет; imperative stress вы́зовите. Takes an accusative object; the imperative asks for an ambulance to be summoned.
language_specific.usage: Соседи addresses several neighbors; скорую is a shortened everyday way to refer to an ambulance.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; contextual imperfective partner выключать. Future forms выключу, выключит; imperative stress вы́ключи. Takes an accusative object; the imperative requests that the light be switched off.
language_specific.usage: Папа identifies a familiar singular addressee; перед сном indicates when to do it.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person plural imperative.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; contextual perfective partner вымыть. Present forms мою, моет; imperative stress мо́йте. Takes an accusative object; the imperfective imperative gives a general instruction.
language_specific.usage: Дети addresses a group; перед едой makes the instruction habitual.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; contextual imperfective partner мыть. Future forms вымою, вымоет; imperative stress вы́мой. Takes an accusative object; the imperative requests completion before this meal.
language_specific.usage: Аня is a familiar singular addressee; the ready meal makes the request immediate.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person plural or polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; contextual perfective partner пройти. Present forms прохожу, проходит; imperative stress проходи́те. Here it invites motion on foot into a room or onward; the prefix про- indicates movement through or past a boundary. The base ходить is multidirectional or repeated motion on foot; this invitation refers to one movement into or through a space.
language_specific.usage: The вы-form politely invites the listener to enter or proceed to the waiting doctor.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is давать. Future forms include дам, дашь; дай is stressed. Takes an accusative object and a dative recipient; requests a completed transfer.
language_specific.usage: The singular imperative suits the family address мама; пожалуйста softens the request.

common.sentence: Анна Сергеевна, возьмите, пожалуйста, мой билет.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is брать. Future forms include возьму, возьмёте; возьми́те has ending stress. Takes an accusative object; requests a completed action.
language_specific.usage: The polite imperative fits the name and patronymic and the request with пожалуйста.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is показывать. Future forms include покажу, покажешь; покажи́ has ending stress. Takes an accusative object and a dative viewer; requests a completed action.

common.sentence: Официант, принесите нам ещё воды, пожалуйста.

language_specific.morphology: Genitive singular feminine; воды́ has ending stress, as does the nominative вода́.
language_specific.usage: With принести, the genitive can indicate an unspecified quantity; ещё asks for more.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person plural imperative, addressed to Маша and her brother.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is открывать. Future forms include открою, откроете; откро́йте has stem stress. Takes an accusative object; requests a completed action.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is закрывать. Future forms include закрою, закроешь; закро́й has stem stress. Takes an accusative object; requests a completed action.

language_specific.morphology: Reflexive second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; the contextual perfective partner is сесть. Present forms include сажусь, садишься; сади́сь has ending stress. It takes no direct object; here it invites the addressee to sit down.
language_specific.usage: Рядом с governs the instrumental: со мной means next to me.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is ждать. Future forms include подожду, подождёте; подожди́те has ending stress. The accusative минуту expresses duration; the request is to wait briefly.
language_specific.usage: The polite form and пожалуйста suit the request to the doctor.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is говорить. Future forms include скажу, скажешь; скажи́ has ending stress. Takes an accusative thing said and a dative recipient; requests the information once.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person plural or polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is повторять. Future forms include повторю, повторите; the imperative повтори́те has ending stress. The thing to repeat can be omitted when understood; the request concerns one repetition.
language_specific.usage: The polite form with пожалуйста asks the listener to repeat what the speaker did not hear clearly.

language_specific.morphology: Comparative form of the adverb медленно; it modifies говори.
language_specific.usage: The comparison is with the listener's current speed of speech.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person plural or polite singular imperative, used as a formula.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is извинять. Future forms include извиню, извините; the imperative извини́те has ending stress. The person excused may be omitted; the formula introduces a request.
language_specific.usage: Извините politely gets a stranger's attention before asking for directions.

common.sentence: Извини, Маша, я забыл твой номер.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative, used as an apology.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is извинять. Future forms include извиню, извинишь; извини́ has ending stress. The person excused may be omitted; the formula apologizes for the stated oversight.
language_specific.usage: The singular form suits the familiar address Маша and твой.

common.sentence: Сынок, не открывай дверь незнакомым людям.

language_specific.morphology: Negated second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; the contextual perfective partner is открыть. Present forms include открываю, открываешь; открыва́й has stem stress. Takes an accusative object; here the negative command gives a general rule.
language_specific.usage: The dative незнакомым людям identifies the people to whom the door must not be opened.

language_specific.morphology: Negated second-person plural imperative.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; no simple aspectual partner is needed for this use. Present forms include шумлю, шумите; the imperative шуми́те has ending stress. It takes no direct object; the command asks the children to keep quiet now.

common.sentence: Миша, не уходи, я сейчас вернусь.

language_specific.morphology: Negated second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; the contextual perfective partner is уйти. Present forms include ухожу, уходишь; уходи́ has ending stress. Underlying ходить is a nondirectional motion verb; the prefix у- marks movement away. Уходить can refer to a single departure or repeated departures. Personal departure normally suggests walking, but transport is possible and the means is unspecified here. It takes no direct object; the command asks Миша to stay.

language_specific.usage: This warning draws attention to the hot tea.

language_specific.morphology: Comparative form of скоро, used here as an urgent call to act quickly.
language_specific.usage: The exclamation and the child's condition make the call urgent.

language_specific.morphology: Accusative singular feminine; direct object of принеси.
Nominative singular feminine noun phrase; нужна agrees with помощь.
language_specific.usage: Скорая помощь is the usual expression for emergency medical help or an ambulance.

common.sentence: В музее нельзя есть и пить.

language_specific.morphology: Infinitive governed by нельзя.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; выпить is a contextual perfective partner for drinking a quantity. Present forms include пью, пьёшь; пить is monosyllabic. It can take an accusative object, omitted here; нельзя prohibits the activity.
language_specific.usage: Нельзя governs the infinitives есть and пить and expresses a prohibition in the museum.

language_specific.morphology: Infinitive governed by можно.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is садиться. Future forms include сяду, сядешь; сесть is monosyllabic. It takes no direct object; here it refers to taking a seat.
language_specific.usage: Можно with an infinitive asks permission to perform the action.
Там points to a location away from the speaker, in contrast with здесь in the question.

language_specific.morphology: Доброе and утро are neuter singular forms; the adjective agrees with the noun.
language_specific.usage: This morning greeting suits the respectful address by name and patronymic.

language_specific.morphology: Добрый and вечер are masculine singular forms; the adjective agrees with the noun.
language_specific.usage: This evening greeting suits the respectful address by name and patronymic.

language_specific.morphology: Genitive singular feminine forms; спокойной agrees with ночи.
language_specific.usage: This farewell is used when someone is going to sleep.

common.sentence: Как ваше имя? — Меня зовут Ольга.

language_specific.morphology: Third-person plural present used impersonally in the naming construction.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; no simple perfective partner is used for this naming sense. Present forms include зову, зовут; зову́т has ending stress. The construction takes the person named in the accusative and their name in the nominative.
language_specific.usage: Меня зовут Ольга gives the speaker's name; the question uses ваше for polite address.

common.sentence: Меня зовут Нина. Я не поняла.

language_specific.morphology: Negated feminine singular past; Нина identifies the speaker.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is понимать. Future forms include пойму, поймёшь; the past feminine поняла́ has ending stress. It can take an accusative object, omitted here; the speaker reports that she did not understand.

language_specific.usage: По-русски identifies the language in which the speaker asks for a word.

language_specific.morphology: Reflexive third-person singular present; agrees with слово.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; no simple perfective partner for this habitual pronunciation use. Present forms include произносится, произносятся; произно́сится has stem stress. It takes no direct object; the question asks about the word's usual pronunciation.

language_specific.usage: Правильно modifies понял; the speaker checks whether he understood the address correctly.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular feminine; the thing whose availability is asked about.
language_specific.usage: Карта города means a map of the city; города is genitive.

language_specific.morphology: Instrumental singular feminine; identifies the means of payment.
language_specific.usage: Оплатить картой means to pay by card.

language_specific.morphology: Accusative singular masculine inanimate; direct object of дайте.
language_specific.usage: Чек за покупку is the receipt for the purchase.
Спасибо за takes the accusative to name what the speaker is thankful for.

language_specific.morphology: Plural or polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Включить is perfective; its imperfective partner is включать. Second conjugation: включу́, включи́шь. It takes an accusative object, here свет. The imperative requests a completed action.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is входить. Future forms include войду, войдёте; войди́те has ending stress. This unidirectional motion verb normally refers to entry on foot; во- signals movement inside. It takes no direct object; the request concerns one entry.
language_specific.usage: The polite imperative and пожалуйста address the doctor respectfully.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Imperfective; пойти is a contextual perfective partner for setting off. Present forms include иду, идёшь; иди́ has ending stress. This unprefixed unidirectional motion verb refers to movement on foot; сюда gives the direction toward the speaker. It takes no direct object.

language_specific.morphology: Comparative form of the adverb тихо; it modifies говорите.
language_specific.usage: The request asks the addressee or addressees to speak more quietly because the child is asleep.

language_specific.morphology: Second-person plural or polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Perfective; the contextual imperfective partner is оставлять. Future forms include оставлю, оставите; оста́вьте has stem stress. Takes an accusative object; the request is to leave the bag in the indicated place.
language_specific.usage: У with the genitive двери identifies the place near the door.
